Q1: 0.70 because known REDs from the prior patch should not be deferred when stability is a prerequisite for a fast train.
Q2: c (both), because bare-flock users bypass gpu-q (requiring a wrapper), but gpu-q is the fleet-wide infrastructure that must enforce it defensively.
Q3: wasted-GPU-minutes, because a lock held for 1 minute at 90% idle is better than a lock held for 10 minutes at 50% idle; absolute time matters.

Q5: yes, because CPU and architecture-independent tasks should produce identical results for the same binary sha, allowing parallel offloading.
Q6: split-X1, because achieving <=4h purely in automation is different from manual fix cycles; budget should distinguish automation speed from human intervention.
Q7: FT-1, FT-2, FT-3, FT-7, FT-10 must land first because X2 relies on the lock being measured and optimized (FT-1,2,3,7) and X1 requires the ledger to measure itself (FT-10).

DESIGN_VERDICT=PASS-WITH-FIXES | Q1=0.71 (defer to 0.71 except #3951 oracle in 0.70); Q2=c; Q3=both; Q4=no; Q5=conditional; Q6=split-X1; Q7=FT-1, FT-2, FT-3, FT-4, FT-5, FT-7, FT-8, FT-9, FT-10, FT-12.

Rulings & Rationales:
- Q1 (0.71 / defer except #3951): 0.70 is themed around release train speed and lock efficiency; carrying low-bit kernel admissions (#3963, #3953, #3960) and MoE fixes (#3987) risks unpredictable debugging cycles, whereas #3951 oracle attribution is already resolved via operator rule (a).
- Q2 (c - both): Enforcing refusal in both fleet-wide gpu-q and aprender repository wrappers (scripts/gpu_test.sh, apr_locked, gpu_exclusive_run.sh) ensures bare-flock scripts cannot bypass compilation-outside-lock discipline.
- Q3 (both): Idle fraction samples in-lock utilization, while wasted GPU-minutes (queue depth * lock duration) measures systemic contention and fleet throughput drag.
- Q4 (no): FT-6 is an experimental pilot that changes no 0.70 lock policy and produces zero release velocity improvement in 0.70.
- Q5 (conditional): CPU legs may migrate across hosts only if binary SHA256 and target CPU ISA/microarchitecture match identically, and evidence explicitly records both host IDs, SHA256, and CPU flags; GPU legs remain strictly host-bound.
- Q6 (split-X1): Split X1 into <= 4h for the automated execution path and a separate budget for triage/fix cycles, avoiding human fix times contaminating release train automation metrics.
- Q7 (FT-1, FT-2, FT-3, FT-4, FT-5, FT-7, FT-8, FT-9, FT-10, FT-12): All hygiene, instrumentation, sharding, CI census, publish drain simulation, duration ledgering, and debt ratchet slice 1 gates must be operational prior to cutting the 0.70 release branch.

FT-1 is owner-free and falsifiable, baseline is measured (#3986, 1.5 min compile in 25 min suite), but proof only tests gpu-q and omits in-repo bare-flock wrappers (scripts/gpu_exclusive_run.sh, apr_locked).

FT-4 proof is partially vacuous: it validates receipt metadata and rejection on mismatched arch, but fails to assert that risk cells actually execute or that pre-screen REDs trigger required host reproduction before ticketing.

FT-6 is owner-free, falsifiable, baseline is cited (binary mutex), and proof tests output sha256 equivalence and planted perturbation failure. However, it is an out-of-scope pilot for a speed release that changes no lock policy.
